name: What is the difference between curbless and low-threshold walk-in showers?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a curbless walk-in shower and a low-threshold walk-in shower, and which one is better for a remodel?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a curbless walk-in shower and a low-threshold walk-in shower, and which one is better for a remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main difference is the entry height. A curbless walk-in shower has no step at the entrance, so the bathroom floor flows directly into the shower. A low-threshold shower still has a small curb or raised edge, usually to help contain water with less structural change. Curbless showers are popular in modern luxury remodels because they create a clean, seamless look and improve access. However, they are more demanding to build because the floor must be sloped correctly, waterproofed thoroughly, and designed around drain placement and framing depth. Low-threshold showers are often easier and less expensive to install, especially in remodels where the existing floor structure limits how much can be lowered. The better choice depends on accessibility goals, water control, budget, and whether the home can support the extra construction needed for a true flush entry.
acceptedAnswer.description: A curbless walk-in shower has no raised step at the entry, while a low-threshold shower has a small curb or lip. Curbless designs are easier to access and create a seamless look, but they usually require more floor work, precise waterproofing, and proper drain planning. Low-threshold showers are simpler to build.
